findings.title: T13's "store-recorded samples only" fallback makes T14 unpassable and contradicts the design's discovery premise
findings.description: The first bullet of T13 says: if no 320 result-discovery surface exists, "scope this task to the store-recorded samples only and note the gap rather than inventing a new file-walk (ask the Project Manager…)." But there is no 320 surface for enumerating unsampled results by `JudgeConfigId` — `capture.py` only has `resolve_target` (resolves one target, by index/type) and `read_review_frontmatter`; `store.list_samples` enumerates *sampled* verdicts. So the fallback is what an implementer will actually take. That fallback is mutually exclusive with T14's "Pruned review file: a matching judge result's review file has been deleted since graduation → that target is skipped, counted, WARNING logged" (and the T13 "non-empty-offers" guarantee is only meaningful over unsampled *files* not in the store). A "store-recorded samples only" implementation cannot know which matching files exist or were deleted, so T14's pruned-file case has nothing to assert against — T13/T14 are a contradictory, untestable pair. This also undercuts the design's "residual sampling" premise, which is explicitly about *unsampled* judge results kept producing data (an offer set over already-sampled data would "freeze" agreement, defeating the feature). Fix: drop the store-only fallback, and make T13 explicit that a bounded review-file discovery helper is *required* (scan `project-documents/user/reviews`, reusing 320's `read_review_frontmatter`/`derive_judge_config_id` to match the exact `JudgeConfigId`, then exclude refs already in the store) — a bounded, DRY reuse of 320's primitives, not a new 320 capability. The success criteria it unblocks: the non-empty-offers guarantee, the pruned-file failure mode, and the lapsed-vs-exhausted distinction.

findings.title: T7's `classify_direction` precedence contradicts the floor-asymmetry success criterion
findings.description: T7 lists the precedence as: (1) `n < floor → INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, (2) `not versioned → INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`, (3) graduate, (4) `match_rate <= tighten_rate → TIGHTEN`, (5) HOLD. Step 1 is unconditional, so a below-floor, low-match-rate cell returns `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` before step 4 is reached — yet T7's own Success line and T8's "Tightening is not floor-gated: `n < floor` with a low match rate returns `TIGHTEN`, not `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`" (and the design's direction-bands table, which the table's `n >= floor` HOLD qualifier confirms) require that cell to be `TIGHTEN`. Implemented literally per the numbered order, T7 fails T8's stated regression. The correct precedence is: unversioned → `TIGHTEN` (not floor-gated) → graduate (floor-gated) → else `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` if `n < floor` → else `HOLD`. Fix: rewrite T7's precedence so the `TIGHTEN` test runs before the `n < floor` → `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` branch. (I'm not calling this a design FAIL — the design's prose, success criteria, and failure-modes row all fix the intended behavior; only the T7 enumeration is wrong — but it is a real defect to correct before implementation.)

findings.title: The runtime-drawn-model (180-pool) clause of the `model_dimension_note` has no task
findings.description: The design's Technical Decision "The (template, model) ↔ (template, step) mismatch is surfaced per recommendation" requires that where a step draws its model at runtime (a 180 pool), the note states the threshold *cannot* track the drawn model and the recommendation does not apply to that step. T9 specifies only a static per-cell note ("holds for this template paired with this model… choose model and threshold together"), and T16 tests only "non-empty `model_dimension_note`." Nothing instructs detecting a runtime-drawn/pool model (or its absence) and appending that limitation, so that sentence of the success criterion is left unaddressed. Even if the template surface has no model-pool field today, the task should decide and state how the note is worded for pool-drawn steps (e.g., a constant limitation sentence keyed off the config, never fabricated per-cell) so the criterion is demonstrably met rather than silently dropped.

findings.title: T13 presumes a 320 result-discovery surface that does not exist
findings.description: Separately from the fallback contradiction: T13 says "reuse 320's existing result-discovery surface rather than re-implementing a review-file scan." No such surface exists (verified: `capture.py` exposes only `resolve_target` and frontmatter reading; `store` exposes only `list_samples`). An implementer told to "reuse" it has nothing to reuse and, per CLAUDE.md, must not invent a new unbounded file-walk. The task should state plainly that discovering unsampled results *requires* adding a bounded discovery helper to `graduation.py` (reusing `read_review_frontmatter` + `derive_judge_config_id`), so scope is explicit and DRY. This is the same location as the FAIL above but is a distinct, independent defect that remains even after the fallback is removed.

findings.title: T2's fixture approach for `_template_content_hash` is underspecified
findings.description: T2 says to build "two `ReviewTemplate` fixtures identical except `judge`," but `_template_content_hash(template_name)` resolves via `get_template(name)` against the shipped template registry, so an in-memory `ReviewTemplate` fixture is not directly consumable. T8's threshold-read tests face the same issue. The task should specify the mechanism (monkeypatch `squadron.review.templates.get_template`, or register a temp template) so a junior implementer doesn't build fixtures the function can't see. The `derive_judge_config_id` end-to-end sub-bullet (threshold edit → same `template_content_hash`; prompt edit → new) is the one that most needs this clarified.

findings.title: Coverage, sequencing, and test-with discipline are otherwise sound
findings.description: Every design success criterion that is *not* flagged above has a tracing task: advisory/no-mutation (T9/T10/T15/T16 byte-identical asserts), floor-gated loosening and stated floor (T7/T8/T15), non-empty-offers and exhausted/pruned/lapsed cases (T13/T14), per-recommendation model-dimension note (T9/T15/T16), version-identity + unversioned refusal (T2/T7/T8), version-scoped graduation with full `JudgeConfigId` (T3/T11/T12/T13), the hash-narrowing regression in both directions (T1/T2/T17 step 5), surface-agnostic core and strict checks (T3/T16/T17), 321 consumed unchanged, and the no-migration `graduated_config` envelope extension (verified compatible with `models.py`). Each implementation task (T1,T3,T5,T7,T9,T11,T13,T15) is immediately followed by its test task, config keys are registered (T5) before the core that reads them (T7/T9), and the hash narrowing lands first as the design requires. The 17 tasks and single file are proportionate to the slice; there is no scope creep and no NFR that would require a load test. No NFR/load-test gap applies.

structured_findings.summary: T13's "store-recorded samples only" fallback makes T14 unpassable and contradicts the design's discovery premise
T7's `classify_direction` precedence contradicts the floor-asymmetry success criterion
The runtime-drawn-model (180-pool) clause of the `model_dimension_note` has no task
T13 presumes a 320 result-discovery surface that does not exist
T2's fixture approach for `_template_content_hash` is underspecified
